title: Infusion duration, volume infused so far and finish time
blurb: Work out how long an infusion will take, when it will finish, and how much has gone in or is left.
question: A 500 mL bag of 5% glucose is started at 0930 and runs through a pump at 80 mL per hour. At what time will it finish?

teach.body: Formal rule: time (hours) = volume (mL) ÷ rate (mL per hour); volume infused = rate × time running; volume left = bag volume − volume infused. Plain English: the same three numbers (volume, rate, time) answer every question; you just solve for the missing one. The trickiest part is turning decimal hours into hours and minutes on the 24-hour clock.

teach.h: Worked example: Ms Byrne on an acute medical unit
teach.body: Siobhan Byrne, 45, has 5% glucose 500 mL started at 0930, running at 80 mL per hour. Time = 500 ÷ 80 = 6.25 hours. 0.25 hours × 60 = 15 minutes, so 6 hours 15 minutes. 0930 + 6 h = 1530; + 15 min = 1545. Sense-check: 80 mL per hour for about 6 hours is about 480 mL, so just over 6 hours is right.

teach.caption: And the reverse: 30 minutes is 0.5 h, not 0.3 h.

teach.text: Reading the decimal as minutes. 6.25 hours is 6 hours 15 minutes, not 6 hours 25 minutes; 12.5 hours is 12 hours 30 minutes, not 12 hours 50. Going the other way, 4 hours 45 minutes is 4.75 hours, not 4.45.

teach.h: Bag started 0700 at 125 mL per hour (1000 mL)

teach.body: On the 24-hour clock, if your answer passes 2400, subtract 24 hours. An infusion started at 2130 that lasts 12 hours 30 minutes ends at 2130 + 1230 = 3400, which is 1000 the next morning. Write times as four digits with no colon (0930, 1545), as charts do.

items.label: when a finish time passes midnight

items: Time = volume ÷ rate; volume infused = rate × time.
Volume left = bag volume − volume infused.
Decimal hours × 60 gives minutes: 0.25 h = 15 min.
Past midnight: subtract 2400 from the clock time.

summary: You can now work out how long an infusion will run, when it will finish on the 24-hour clock, and how much has been infused or is left. You can also convert between decimal hours and hours and minutes without the classic slip.

A.q: A 1000 mL bag of 0.9% sodium chloride is running through a pump at 80 mL per hour. How many hours will the bag take to finish? Write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This writes 12 hours 30 minutes as 12.3 hours.
whyNot.2: This divides rate by volume, the inverted fraction (0.08 rounds to 0.1).

A.q: A 500 mL bag of 5% glucose is started at 0930 and runs through a pump at 80 mL per hour. At what time will it finish?
A.why: Time = 500 ÷ 80 = 6.25 hours = 6 hours 15 minutes. 0930 + 6 h 15 min = 1545.

whyNot.0: This reads 6.25 hours as 6 hours 25 minutes.
whyNot.2: This rounds 6.25 hours up to 6.5 hours.

A.q: An infusion started at 0800 is running through a pump at 120 mL per hour. What volume will have been infused by 1130? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.1: This writes 3 hours 30 minutes as 3.3 hours.
whyNot.3: This rounds the time up to 4 hours.

B.q: A 1000 mL bag has been running through a pump at 100 mL per hour for 4 hours 45 minutes. What volume remains in the bag? Please use the correct unit.
B.why: Time = 4.75 hours. Infused = 100 × 4.75 = 475 mL. Remaining = 1000 − 475 = 525 mL.

whyNot.0: This writes 4 hours 45 minutes as 4.45 hours.
whyNot.1: This is the volume infused, not the volume left.

B.q: A 250 mL infusion is running through a pump at 75 mL per hour. How many minutes will it take to finish?

whyNot.0: This gives the time in hours (3.33) but labels it minutes.
whyNot.2: This moves the decimal point in 3.33 instead of multiplying by 60.

B.q: A man is receiving 1 unit of red cells, volume 300 mL, through a pump at 120 mL per hour. How many hours will the transfusion take? Write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.1: This writes 2 hours 30 minutes as 2.3 hours.
whyNot.2: This divides rate by volume, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This uses 100 mL per hour instead of 120.

C.q: A 750 mL infusion is started at 2130 and runs through a pump at 60 mL per hour. At what time will it finish?
C.why: Time = 750 ÷ 60 = 12.5 hours = 12 hours 30 minutes. 2130 + 12 h 30 min = 3400, which is 1000 the next morning.

whyNot.1: This reads 12.5 hours as 12 hours 50 minutes.
whyNot.3: This counts 13 hours instead of 12 hours 30 minutes.

C.q: A 1000 mL bag is started at 0700 at 125 mL per hour. At 1100 the rate is reduced to 100 mL per hour. At what time will the bag finish?

whyNot.0: This is the finish time if the rate had stayed at 125 mL per hour.
whyNot.2: This runs the whole 1000 mL at 100 mL per hour from 0700.
whyNot.3: This runs the whole 1000 mL at 100 mL per hour from 1100.

C.q: An infusion runs through a pump at 90 mL per hour from 0815 to 1345. What volume has been infused? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This writes 5 hours 30 minutes as 5.3 hours.
whyNot.1: This rounds the time up to 6 hours.

reteach.title: Decimals to minutes
reteach.question: An infusion will take 6.25 hours. How many hours and minutes is that?

blocks.body: Keep the 6 hours. 0.25 × 60 = 15 minutes. So 6.25 hours is 6 hours 15 minutes.

blocks.text: Reading 6.25 hours as 6 hours 25 minutes adds 10 minutes that do not exist.

explain.body: 600 mL at 150 mL per hour takes 600 ÷ 150 = 4 hours.

test.q: A 600 mL infusion is running through a pump at 150 mL per hour. How many hours will it take to finish?

whyNot.1: This divides rate by volume, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This misreads the rate as 15 mL per hour.

test.q: How many minutes are there in 0.75 hours?

whyNot.0: This reads the decimal as minutes.
whyNot.1: This moves the decimal point instead of multiplying by 60.
whyNot.3: This is 0.25 hours; 0.75 hours is three quarters of an hour.

explain.h: Adding hours and minutes to a clock time
explain.body: Add the hours, then the minutes; carry 60 minutes into an hour. 1345 + 5 h = 1845; + 30 min = 1915.

test.q: An infusion is started at 1345 and will run for 5 hours 30 minutes. At what time will it finish?

whyNot.0: This adds 530 as a plain number; minutes past 59 must carry into the hour.
whyNot.1: This adds the hours but not the 30 minutes.
whyNot.2: This adds 6 hours instead of 5 hours 30 minutes.
